scope.method: Figma masters extracted read-only via figmosha2 into audit/raw/parity/*.json; React side read from src/components/**. No mutations.

summary.headline: The port is materially healthier than feared. Button/IconButton/Badge/SeverityBadge/Row geometry is pixel-exact against the masters. Four findings change layout; the largest single risk is the table row height (68 vs 56).

findings.figma: TableRow master (10298:18440) variant=default is 56px tall; TableCell (10298:18423) and TableHeaderCell (10298:18358) are both 56px. Master is internally inconsistent: the Table master (10302:18481) contains TableRow instances overridden to 56 and 60.
findings.code: src/components/Table/Table.tsx:16 TABLE_ROW_MAX_HEIGHT_PX = 68; src/components/TableRow/TableRow.module.css:13 height: var(--table-row-height, 68px); src/components/TableCell/TableCell.module.css:7-8 height/max-height 68px
findings.verdict: code-wrong — the master says 56 and the brief makes the master ground truth. Caveat: the code's fill-to-available behaviour (rows stretch to fill the card, capped at the max) is a deliberate improvement with no Figma equivalent, so only the 68 cap is in question, not the mechanism.
findings.proposed: Set TABLE_ROW_MAX_HEIGHT_PX = 56 and change both CSS fallbacks to 56px. If the owner prefers 68 as the real intent, update the TableRow master instead and normalise the stray 60px instance inside the Table master.
findings.blastRadius: Every table screen: aegis TrucksPage, TrailersPage, DriversPage, and the two Maintenance & repair screens (Figma Frames 6,7,8,10,11,12). 12px per row x 8 rows = ~96px of vertical shift per table. This is the single most template-relevant finding.

findings.figma: TableCell (10298:18423) content=textStrong title uses text/label/sm — 13px / weight 600 / line-height 1.15, rendering a 15px line box. content=text title uses text/body/sm — 13px / weight 500 / line-height 1.5, a 20px line box.
findings.code: src/components/TableCell/TableCellText.tsx:12 emphasis?: 'default' | 'strong'; TableCellText.module.css:43-48 — `strong` changes only color (--color-text-strong) and keeps body/sm 500 at line-height 1.5.
findings.verdict: code-wrong — TableCellText.tsx:20 asserts Figma split textStrong out 'purely because Figma can't parameterize a variant's color', but the master also changes weight (500->600) and line-height (1.5->1.15). The stated rationale is contradicted by the master data.
findings.proposed: Make emphasis='strong' apply the full text/label/sm token set (font-size, weight, line-height, letter-spacing), not just colour.
findings.blastRadius: Any table with a primary-identifier column (rig ID, truck number, driver name) — Trucks, Trailers, Drivers, both Maintenance screens. Changes the cell's line box by 5px, so it interacts with TABLE-001; fix them together.

findings.figma: TableHeaderCell (10298:18358) is a fixed 56px tall with padding 0/16/0/16 (no vertical padding). TableRow variant=header is 44px tall.
findings.code: src/components/TableHeaderCell/TableHeaderCell.module.css:2 padding: var(--space-12) var(--space-16); no height is set, so the header row height derives from padding + line box: 12 + ~15 + 12 = ~39px (+1px border).
findings.verdict: code-wrong on height — the rendered header is ~39px against a master that specifies 44px (row) / 56px (cell). Note the master is itself inconsistent here, so the target value needs the owner's call.
findings.proposed: Give the header row an explicit height token and set vertical padding to 0, matching the master's centring model. Resolve the master's own 44-vs-56 contradiction first (see TROW-002).
findings.blastRadius: The header band of all six table screens. Smaller than TABLE-001 but compounds with it — together they set the table's whole vertical rhythm, which is exactly what an L3 template would freeze.

findings.figma: No Figma master — layout primitives are code-only (L1).
findings.code: src/components/Stack/Stack.module.css:4 has min-width: 0. src/components/Box/Box.module.css has only box-sizing — no min-width: 0. docs/components/layout.md:53-54 claims 'min-width: 0 is baked into both so flex children can shrink (text truncation, tables) without overflowing.'
findings.verdict: code-wrong — the doc states the intent, Stack implements it, Box does not. A Box used as a flex child will refuse to shrink below its content, breaking the exact truncation case the doc promises.
findings.proposed: Add min-width: 0 to .box in Box.module.css.
findings.blastRadius: Any Box inside a row Stack that contains long text — table cells, card headers, the Headercard title row. Silent today; it surfaces as horizontal overflow the first time real data is longer than the mock copy, which is precisely when aegis switches from placeholders to Supabase rows.

findings.figma: No Figma master — code-only primitive.
findings.code: src/components/Stack/Stack.module.css:38-45 — .columns { flex-direction: row } has specificity (0,1,0); .stack[data-direction='column'] has (0,2,0) and always wins. Stack.tsx:34 defaults direction='column' and Stack.tsx:52 always emits data-direction.
findings.verdict: code-wrong — <Stack columns> alone silently produces a COLUMN whose children get flex: 1 1 0 (equal heights stacked vertically), not equal-width columns. It only works as <Stack direction="row" columns>, which is what both the JSDoc and layout.md happen to show.
findings.proposed: Change the selector to .stack.columns (ties on specificity, wins on source order), or set data-direction={columns ? 'row' : direction} in Stack.tsx.
findings.blastRadius: None today — every current call site passes direction="row". The risk is forward-looking: aegis screen-composition §9 is about to make `columns` mandatory house law, which makes the bare form far more likely to be written. Worth hardening before the templates land, not after.

findings.figma: Modal (10264:14412) scales its internal gap with padding: xs 12/12, sm 16/16, md 20/20, lg 24/24.
findings.code: src/components/Modal/Modal.module.css:6 gap: var(--space-20) is fixed on .modal; lines 41-44 vary only padding.
findings.verdict: code-wrong — only padding='md' matches the master by coincidence; xs, sm and lg all render a 20px gap where the master specifies 12, 16 and 24.
findings.proposed: Move gap into the per-padding rules alongside padding, mirroring the master's 1:1 padding/gap relationship.
findings.blastRadius: No built aegis screen uses Modal yet, so this is free to fix now. It becomes expensive once confirm/edit dialogs land on the Alerts screens.

findings.figma: Card (10033:11096) has padding = none | sm | md | lg only (0 / 12 / 16 / 20). There is no xl variant.
findings.code: src/components/Card/Card.tsx:6 CardPadding includes 'xl'; Card.module.css:25 .card[data-padding='xl'] { padding: var(--space-24) }
findings.verdict: both-defensible — the four shared steps match the master exactly; xl is an extra affordance in code with no designed counterpart. Not a rendering bug, but a template that reaches for padding="xl" would standardise an undesigned value.
findings.proposed: Either add a padding=xl variant to the master (24px, consistent with Modal's lg) or drop 'xl' from CardPadding. Owner's call; the audit's only ask is that the two surfaces agree.
findings.blastRadius: None currently — no call site uses padding="xl". Decide before the templates pick a house padding.

findings.figma: Badge (10036:11182) exposes the icon-presence axis as variant = default | withicon.
findings.code: src/components/Badge/Badge.tsx:15 BadgeIcon = 'default' | 'hasIcon', surfaced as the prop `icon`.
findings.verdict: both-defensible — neither surface follows design-system-conventions. The prop name differs (variant vs icon) and so do the values (withicon vs hasIcon); conventions require identical names/values, reserve `variant` for the style axis (as Button uses it), and mandate lowercase-kebab values. It is really a boolean.
findings.proposed: Make it a boolean on both surfaces: a Figma BOOLEAN property `hasIcon` and a React prop `hasIcon?: boolean`. This is an API change — flag it for triage rather than applying it.
findings.blastRadius: Every Badge call site in the design system and aegis, plus SeverityBadge (which composes Badge). Rendering is unaffected; this is a rename, so it is cheap now and progressively more expensive.

findings.figma: TaskCard (10168:17214) variants are fixed-size frames: context=list 380x200, context=tasks 320x170, context=queue 380x230 (hug, 4 stacked layers).
findings.code: src/components/TaskCard/TaskCard.module.css:1-7 .taskCard { width: 100%; height: 100% } — the card fills its container and never sizes from content.
findings.verdict: both-defensible, and it answers PARITY-AUDIT §6.10 affirmatively: TaskCard does NOT force height from content. Title is one line with ellipsis (line 79), description is clamped to two rows (line 93), and .footer uses margin-top: auto (line 102), so copy length cannot change height.
findings.proposed: No component change. Document the contract: equal height requires a stretching parent (CSS Grid row, or Stack direction="row" columns). height: 100% against an auto-height block parent collapses to content height — that is the one way a consumer can break the 3x3 grid.
findings.blastRadius: aegis TasksPage 3x3 grid (Figma Frame 4). The requirement holds, but it is conditional on the grid container, so the template must own the row sizing.

findings.figma: TableRow (10298:18440) variant=header is 44px tall, but TableHeaderCell (10298:18358) — the component that fills it — is 56px tall. A 56px cell cannot sit in a 44px row.
findings.code: n/a — this is a contradiction internal to Figma.
findings.verdict: figma-wrong — the two masters disagree with each other, so neither can be quoted as ground truth for header height until the owner picks one.
findings.proposed: Decide the header height (44 or 56) and correct whichever master is wrong. THEAD-001 is blocked on this answer.
findings.blastRadius: Indirect — it blocks THEAD-001, which touches the header band of all six table screens.

findings.figma: Card (10033:11096) padding: none=0, sm=12, md=16, lg=20. Modal (10264:14412) padding: xs=12, sm=16, md=20, lg=24. The same step name means a different value on each component — sm is 12 on Card but 16 on Modal; md is 16 vs 20; lg is 20 vs 24.
findings.code: Card.module.css:22-25 and Modal.module.css:41-44 reproduce both scales faithfully.
findings.verdict: figma-wrong — this answers code-side question C2. The offset is NOT a porting error: both masters genuinely disagree, and the React code copies each one correctly. Fixing it therefore requires a Figma change, not a code change.
findings.proposed: Realign the two scales on one shared vocabulary (most likely give Modal a none/sm/md/lg matching Card, or rename Modal's steps), then update code to follow. Until then, document the trap loudly in both component docs.
findings.blastRadius: Any screen composing both — the aegis session notes RigProblemDetail already passes padding="sm" to Modal, getting Card's md. Dangerous precisely because it is invisible: the prop name is identical and nothing errors.

findings.figma: Button (10052:11507) and IconButton (10059:12060) expose state = default | hover | disabled | active. There is NO focus state in either master. Verified geometry: state=active switches the stroke from 1.5/0/0/1.5 (top+left) to 1.5/1.5/1.5/1.5 (full perimeter).
findings.code: Button.module.css:59-66, 84-94 — :focus-visible reuses the active look (inset 0 0 0 1.5px full ring) and sets outline: none. Tertiary instead uses a real outline: 2px solid var(--color-border-focus) with offset 2px (lines 117-121).
findings.verdict: figma-wrong — this answers code-side question C7. The code's ring geometry faithfully matches the master's active state, so the port is correct; the gap is that the master never designed a focus state at all, leaving focus visibility undefined by design. Three different focus recipes across Button variants is the downstream symptom.
findings.proposed: Add an explicit focus state to the Button/IconButton masters and settle one focus recipe system-wide. Note that outline: none paired with an inset ring on a glass surface is the classic WCAG 2.4.7 shape — worth a deliberate ruling for a project whose stated purpose includes proving accessibility. The ring's contrast is a colour question and stays deferred under brief §5.
findings.blastRadius: Every interactive surface on every screen, for keyboard users only. No visual change for mouse users, which is exactly why it survives review.

findings.figma: n/a
findings.code: docs/components/layout.md:58 — the worked example opens with <PageHeader title="Shipments" />. No PageHeader value is exported: src/index.ts:165 exports only the TYPE PageHeaderProps, and the component is the compound Page.Header (src/components/Page/Page.tsx:99).
findings.verdict: doc-stale — the snippet would not compile, and it also violates aegis screen-composition §1 (nothing on the bare Page canvas).
findings.proposed: Rewrite the example to use Page.Header inside the Page contract, or drop the header line entirely. Highest value-per-character fix in this audit: docs are what coding agents imitate, and this one teaches a pattern aegis explicitly rejects.
findings.blastRadius: No rendered output. Affects every future agent-written screen that copies this snippet — which, given how aegis delegates screen work, is the point.

findings.figma: radius/container and radius/panel both resolve to 12 post-1440.
findings.code: docs/components/layout.md:23 — 'radius roles (6 · 8 · 12 · 16)' implies container = 16.
findings.verdict: doc-stale — build/tokens.css shows --radius-container and --radius-panel both aliasing --radius-xl (12). Code is correct.
findings.proposed: Change the doc to (6 · 8 · 12 · 12) or note that panel and container are deliberately the same value today.
findings.blastRadius: None rendered.

findings.figma: Card master (10033:11096) corner radius = 12 on all four padding variants.
findings.code: docs/components/Card.md:32 — 'radius | radius/card -> radius/container -> 16'. Card.module.css:6 correctly uses var(--radius-card), which resolves to 12.
findings.verdict: doc-stale — confirms the suspicion in PARITY-AUDIT §6.1 exactly. Figma, tokens and CSS all agree on 12; only the doc says 16.
findings.proposed: Change 16 to 12 in Card.md:32.
findings.blastRadius: None rendered.

findings.figma: Button (10052:11507) and IconButton (10059:12060) both expose size = xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl.
findings.code: src/components/Button/Button.tsx:8 ButtonSize correctly includes 'xs' and '2xl', but the JSDoc above the size prop says '`sm` · `md` (default) · `lg` · `xl`'. IconButton.tsx:12 carries the same truncated list.
findings.verdict: doc-stale — the type is right, the JSDoc undersells it. IconButton's comment does mention the xs/2xl variant restrictions on the next line, so only the enumeration is wrong.
findings.proposed: Extend both JSDoc lines to the full six-step scale.
findings.blastRadius: None rendered. Matters because JSDoc is what an editor autocomplete shows an agent.

findings.figma: The header label is bound to the text style text/badge-label/sm (13px / 600 / 115%, textCase UPPER).
findings.code: src/components/TableHeaderCell/TableHeaderCell.module.css:28-37 uses the text/label/sm token set plus text-transform: uppercase.
findings.verdict: figma-wrong — 'badge-label' is not an approved typography group. design-system-conventions fixes the grammar to text.<group>.<size> with group in display|heading|body|label. The style is numerically identical to text/label/sm, so the code renders correctly; only the Figma style name is off-vocabulary.
findings.proposed: Rebind the header label to text/label/sm and retire text/badge-label/sm (a figma-safe-edit job, after triage). Verified separately: the master's textCase is UPPER on both node and style, so the code's text-transform: uppercase is correct — not a finding.
findings.blastRadius: None rendered — identical metrics either way. It is a naming-contract fix.

findings.figma: Badge withicon corner radii verified per-corner: 32/6/6/32 at xs and sm, 32/8/8/32 at md and lg.
findings.code: src/components/Badge/Badge.module.css:85,88,91 use var(--radius-5xl) for the icon-side corners.
findings.verdict: code-wrong on tier only — the value (32) matches the master exactly, but --radius-5xl is a primitive. Conventions: components reference semantic or component tokens only, never primitives.
findings.proposed: Add a component token (e.g. radius.badge.icon-side -> radius.5xl) and reference that. Zero visual change.
findings.blastRadius: None — pure token indirection.

findings.figma: Row (10180:18768) corner radius = 4 across all sizes/states.
findings.code: src/components/Row/Row.module.css:7 border-radius: var(--radius-sm) — the 4px primitive.
findings.verdict: code-wrong on tier only — value matches the master; the token tier does not. There is no semantic role at 4px, which is why the primitive got reached for.
findings.proposed: Add a component token radius.row -> radius.sm. Zero visual change.
findings.blastRadius: None — pure token indirection.

findings.figma: Modal master corner radius = 12, matching radius/modal -> radius/container.
findings.code: src/components/Modal/Modal.module.css:5 border-radius: var(--radius-card) — Card's component token, not Modal's.
findings.verdict: code-wrong on tier only — --radius-modal exists and resolves to the same 12, so nothing renders differently; Modal is just borrowing another component's token.
findings.proposed: Swap to var(--radius-modal).
findings.blastRadius: None — identical value.

findings.figma: TableCell icon slots are 16x16; the iconOnly variant hosts a 40x40 action (IconButton size=xl); the badge variant hosts a 47x27 Badge (size=sm).
findings.code: src/components/TableCell/TableCellText.module.css:13,26 set font-size: 16px as raw px to drive the 1em icon box.
findings.verdict: code-wrong on tier only — 16px matches the master exactly, but conventions say app code never writes raw px. There is no icon-size token scale yet, which is the real gap.
findings.proposed: Either introduce an icon-size token scale or leave with an explicit comment. Lowest priority item here. Useful side-effect for aegis: this pins table badges to Badge size="sm" and table row actions to IconButton size="xl".
findings.blastRadius: None — value is correct.

findings.figma: TaskCard context=queue front card is 200px tall (ghosts at 200, offset 10px/20px narrower per layer).
findings.code: src/components/TaskCard/TaskCard.module.css:160 .queue .shadow { min-height: 180px }
findings.verdict: code-wrong — a 20px shortfall against the master's front-card height, and only a floor rather than a height, so it usually stretches past it anyway.
findings.proposed: Raise to 200px, or confirm the floor is deliberately lower than the design height.
findings.blastRadius: aegis DashboardPage 'what's next' widget (Figma Frame 9) only, and only when the container is short enough for the floor to bind.

findings.figma: TableRow exposes variant = header | default and state = default | active | hover | danger | success | selected.
findings.code: src/components/TableRow/TableRow.tsx:7,12 expose only status?: 'danger' | 'success' and selected?: boolean. Header-vs-body comes from whether Table places the row in <thead> or <tbody>; hover/active are real :hover / :focus-within.
findings.verdict: both-defensible, and the code is the better citizen — design-system-conventions explicitly says not to encode interaction state as a variant, since state is CSS pseudo-classes in code. The divergence is documented in the source.
findings.proposed: No change. Recording it so the next audit does not re-flag it as missing variants.
findings.blastRadius: None.

findings.figma: No Figma master exists for either layout primitive. The component sets named 'Stack' (4009:2477) and 'GridFour' (4009:2308) are Phosphor ICONS with Format/Weight axes, not layout components.
findings.code: src/components/Grid/Grid.module.css and src/components/Stack/Stack.module.css — code-only L1 primitives.
findings.verdict: both-defensible — layout primitives legitimately have no visual master. Recording it so 'missing from Figma' is not mistaken for a gap. Grid itself checks out: minmax(0, 1fr) columns with min-width: 0 on both .grid and .item.
findings.proposed: No change. Note for future audits: do not diff Stack/Grid against the same-named icon sets.
findings.blastRadius: None.
